source: Goehler, Frey, Howard (2016) A model-based approach to associate complexity and robustness in engineering systems, Research in Engineering Design
finding: This is a simulation study, not a human experiment. It tests Suh's independence axiom against robustness. The axiom holds in general only for nominal-is-best requirements. It fails for max-is-best and min-is-best requirements. A machining example shows a coupled design that is more robust than its uncoupled twin.
numbers: 250 modelled design architectures (Monte Carlo, hierarchical probability model). For max/min-is-best, robustness depends most on the level of contradiction between coupled FRs, p = 1.4e-36.
quote: this study proves this not to be the case for max-/min-is-best requirements
limits: Only the abstract page was read this session; the full text is behind a paywall and the MIT DSpace PDF returned HTTP 429. Effect sizes and model details not seen. Robustness here means variation, not design effort. Models are synthetic.
agent_relevance: Counts against a rule that says always make the matrix triangular. Coupling is bad for tuning effort but can be good for robustness, so the scaffold should treat decoupling as a preference, not a hard gate.

source: Goehler et al. (2016), second attempt at full text (MIT DSpace and Springer PDF)
finding: Full text could not be opened: MIT DSpace PDF returned 429, Springer returned a paywall page. Gap 4 for this paper stays partly open.
limits: Access failure, not evidence about the paper.

source: Hirschi and Frey (2002) Cognition and complexity: An experiment on the effect of coupling in parameter design, Research in Engineering Design 13:123-131 (journal abstract)
finding: Journal abstract confirms the ICAD numbers. At 2 inputs by 2 outputs coupling had only a moderate effect. As size grew, coupling had a drastic effect on solution procedure and completion time. Time for coupled tasks rose geometrically from 2x2 to 5x5. Results are discussed through information-processing models of human cognition.
numbers: Human subjects, simple graphical interface. N=12 and 3.4^n growth come from the earlier opened ICAD text (b01-b03), not from this page. OpenAlex lists 77 citing works (count only, list not retrieved).
quote: the effect of coupling among variables has a drastic effect on the solution procedures and the completion time
limits: Only abstract opened here; full journal text paywalled and core.ac.uk returned 403. Effect sizes and robustness checks beyond the ICAD version unknown.
agent_relevance: Cognitive-load style cost of coupling is the one human anchor. Suggests testing whether an agent's search cost also grows geometrically with coupled size.

source: Grogan and de Weck (2016) Collaboration and complexity: an experiment on the effect of multi-actor coupled design, Research in Engineering Design
finding: A different group replicated the geometric growth of completion time with problem size for highly coupled tasks, using a parameter-design surrogate task. New result: team size effect is independent of problem size. Collaboration took a large share of effort.
numbers: 10 groups of 3 subjects, 42 design tasks each; variable problem size, coupling and team size. Two-level regression. Collaboration share: pairs 50-60% of time and 70-80% of cost; triads 60-80% of time and 90% of cost.
limits: Abstract only. Same university as Hirschi and Frey (MIT), different authors, a design-team variant not a strict repeat. Pairs and triads, not individuals. Does not test the axiom itself or other methods.
agent_relevance: Closes gap 8 in part: the main time-growth finding has one independent replication. Also warns that coordination between several agents adds its own cost on top of coupling.

source: Jiang and Luo (2026) Design Structure Matrix Modularization with Large Language Models, arXiv 2604.28018 (full text read)
finding: Authors call it a knowledge paradox. Domain knowledge helped DSM sequencing in their earlier paper but hurts modularization on larger DSMs. Their explanation is semantic misalignment: visible node names make the LLM group by function, which differs from the purely structural objective. The explanation is a hypothesis, not tested by intervention.
numbers: Claude-Sonnet-4.6, GPT-5.2, Qwen-3.5-Plus; 5 cases; k=0 vs k=1; 10 trials x 30 iterations each; temperature 1.0. Claude: UCAV gap 0.9% (k=1) vs 2.0% (k=0); Kodak and Brake no change; HeatEx +5.4% penalty; Helicopter +3.6% penalty, 0 of 10 runs hit the SA reference with k=1 vs 10 of 10 with k=0 (TotalCost 1371 +/- 0).
quote: domain knowledge consistently and substantially impairs performance
limits: Same authors as the sequencing paper. SA reference is not provably optimal for larger cases. Cases have at most 19 elements. The separation appears within the first iterations and persists.
agent_relevance: Guidance that matches the task's own objective can still hurt if it pulls the model toward a different grouping. Scaffold hints should be optional and switchable per task, and checked against the scoring rule.

source: Jiang and Luo (2026) Table 1 case sizes, with density arithmetic check
finding: Case sizes recovered from Table 1 and checked by density = E/(N(N-1)). Helicopter is the largest case at N=19, not 14. HeatEx has 17 nodes, Kodak 14, Brake 13, UCAV 12. The earlier critique correction that Helicopter has 14 nodes was wrong: the pdf table columns were misaligned and that reading mixed rows. The text states largest case (Helicopter, n = 19).
limits: Row labels were garbled in text extraction; the assignment follows the density and the text statement.
agent_relevance: Matters only for the claim that the penalty grows with size: the two largest cases (17 and 19) are the ones that suffer.

source: Jiang and Luo (2026) cross-model pattern for knowledge effect
finding: The paradox is not general across models. For GPT and Qwen, knowledge (k=1) gives lower gap in early iterations, but k=0 catches up or passes it later on most cases. The authors read this as capability moderation: a strong model gets distracted by priors, a weaker model gains a shortcut that fades as the solution pool fills. GPT and Qwen also show much higher run-to-run variance, especially on UCAV and Helicopter.
numbers: Same 10 trials x 30 iterations design. Per-model gap tables only in figures, not read as numbers.
limits: Qualitative reading of convergence curves. No test beyond optimization tasks.
agent_relevance: Do not generalise guidance hurts to all scaffolds. The honest reading: guidance may speed early search and hurt final quality for strong models. Measure both early and final scores.

source: Jiang and Luo (2026) limits and contrast with sequencing study
finding: Authors list limits: at most 19 elements, SA reference not provably optimal on larger cases, only three model families, other DSM types (for example physical-interface DSMs) may behave differently. In DSM sequencing, minimising feedback loops matches engineering process logic so knowledge helped; in modularization the structural goal diverges from functional grouping.
numbers: Ablations (input format, objective, solution pool) were all on UCAV with Claude and k=1. Default input is a directed edge list.
limits: Ablation scope is one case and one model.
agent_relevance: Supports the rule: add knowledge only where it is aligned with the objective being scored.

source: Homay (2025) Complexity and Coupling: A Functional Domain Approach, arXiv 2507.09599 (full text read)
finding: The full text has no LLM content, no experiment on requirement rewriting, and no planning-quality measure. It is a definitional argument for placing complexity and coupling in the functional domain. The only data is an unsampled survey of over 100 software engineers, more than 80% of whom judged the two-knob faucet wrongly.
numbers: Survey: over 100 software engineers; more than 80% incorrect. No sampling method, no confidence interval.
limits: Advocacy paper by a single author. This paper cannot be used for gap 6; the LLM argument in the 2026 Homay paper is separate and was not re-opened.
agent_relevance: Gap 6 has no support from this source. Treat solution-neutral FRs help LLMs as untested.

source: Joshi, Shukla, Gandhi (2026) Enterprise AI System Design framework (SSRN 7341198), abstract via Crossref
finding: Abstract text read through Crossref. It claims empirical validation across three case studies, and attributes the numbers to a separate work cited as Joshi 2026a. So the headline figures are not derived in this paper's abstract, and the coupling measure is not defined there. Full text blocked by Cloudflare. Gap 5 stays open.
numbers: Claimed: coupling down 34.2% (p<.01), design iterations down 41%, accessibility compliance 91.7% vs 54.2%, latency down 22% in MLOps governance, zero safety regression. Three cases. No N, no baseline definition.
limits: Preprint; the framework authors report their own results and also build the open-source tool (CoHumAIn AD Four-Domain Mapper). Cites HAICO (Joshi and Shukla 2026), also self-cited. No independent source.
agent_relevance: Do not use. Keep as unverified.

source: O'Hara (2025) Agentic Architecture Mediation for LLM Assistants: Preventing Solution-Jumping with Requirements Elicitation (TechRxiv)
finding: Closest thing found to testing requirements first, solution second on an LLM. A multi-agent Five Whys workflow plus a deterministic evaluator detected solution mismatches in six hand-made antipatterns. It is a detection test, not a measure of better final design.
numbers: Six industry antipatterns, 100% detection of solution mismatches, about $0.01 per session.
limits: Abstract only via Crossref. Six cases, author-built, no baseline LLM without the workflow reported in the abstract. Not solution-neutral FR rewriting as such.
agent_relevance: Weak support for a requirements-first step, and for the split LLM does dialogue, program does evaluation. Gap 6 stays open.

source: Ataei et al. (2025) Elicitron: LLM agent-based simulation for design requirements elicitation, J Computing and Information Science in Engineering
finding: Adjacent to gap 6. Simulated LLM users uncover more latent needs than conventional human interviews in the authors' tests; context-aware agent generation gives more diverse needs; LLMs can classify needs as latent or not.
numbers: Three experiments reported in the abstract; counts and N not in the abstract.
limits: Abstract only via Crossref. It tests need discovery, not whether solution-neutral requirements improve later design.
agent_relevance: Shows LLMs can widen the requirement set; says nothing about decoupling or about downstream quality.

source: Mollajan, Iranmanesh, Khezri, Abazari (2022) Effect of applying independence axiom on an Integrated Manufacturing Information System, SIMULATION (abstract via Crossref)
finding: A simulation outcome test of the independence axiom on one real system. Authors report that fulfilling the independence axiom significantly improved system performance (time in process, resource utilisation) by logistic regression at each decomposition level.
numbers: One real IMIS simulated in Visual SLAM/AweSim; no N or effect size in the abstract; 13 citations per Crossref.
limits: Abstract only. One system, simulated. No human or LLM study. Not independent of the axiom's proponents.
agent_relevance: One more weak positive outcome point for independence on system performance, but a simulation of one system.

source: Independence Measure (IM) using Independence Priority Number (IPN) in Axiomatic Design framework (ASME IMECE 2015, abstract via Crossref)
finding: AD ranks designs only by three classes (uncoupled, decoupled, coupled) and cannot rank two designs in the same class. The paper proposes IPN and IM metrics for degree of coupling to compare robustness.
numbers: No data in the abstract; proposal only.
limits: Abstract only. No validation seen. 0 citations on Crossref.
agent_relevance: Supports using a graded coupling count (computed by program) instead of a three-way label.

source: Sun, Chen, Bakirtzis, Jafarzadeh, Fleming (2026) Functional requirements decomposition in set-based design, Design Science
finding: A four-step formal method to decompose functional requirements for set-based design. It states the gap that SBD literature lacks decomposition guidance. No experiment in the abstract.
limits: Abstract only. Does not use Suh's axioms in the abstract.
agent_relevance: Neighbouring method for keeping alternatives open while decomposing; no evidence value for the independence gaps.

source: Search record, gaps 1-3 (LLM matrix-first scaffold, coupled-tuning blowup with agents, LLM classification of coupling): Crossref queries on 2026-11-19
finding: Crossref queries on axiomatic design plus LLM, coupled design variables plus LLM, and coupling classification plus LLM returned no study that tests any of the three. arXiv export, Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex returned HTTP 429 for most of the session, and WebSearch had run out of budget, so the negative result is weaker than a full search.
numbers: 0 relevant hits in about 12 Crossref queries (results were off-topic: ontologies, polymer agents, requirements tools).
limits: Absence of evidence under throttled search. Crossref indexes abstracts unevenly and preprints late.
agent_relevance: Gaps 1, 2 and 3 remain open and are testable by us.

source: Mobile-phone ergonomics comparison based on the information axiom (World Scientific 2006, Crossref metadata)
finding: Metadata only: an application of the information axiom to a multi-attribute comparison. No abstract available. Fits the earlier finding that information axiom use is multi-criteria selection with no outcome test.

source: Hirschi and Frey (2002) citation-count check (OpenAlex W2145964432)
